metadata.title: R&D Tax Credit Landscape: Q1 2026 Updates & Key Considerations
metadata.author: Cherry Bekaert
metadata.shortDescription:
Tune in to Cherry Bekaert’s Q1 2026 R&D Tax Credit Update, where our knowledgeable team breaks down key opportunities, compliance considerations and recent developments impacting companies of all sizes. 

We also cover the ongoing effects of IRC Section 174 — including required capitalization and amortization of foreign research expenditures — and provide practical insights into navigating both the Section 41 R&D Credit and Section 174A rules. Receive clear guidance on current challenges and upcoming IRS reporting requirements that may affect your business in 2026 and beyond.

What to Expect:
- Learn about the R&D tax credit, including eligibility requirements, qualifying activities and how the credit can benefit businesses across multiple industries.
- Discover considerations for addressing Section 174 capitalization that should have been reported in prior tax years.
- Determine the pros and cons of amending 2022 – 2024 tax returns for eligible small businesses that capitalized R&E in those years.
- Gain insights on states that do and do not conform to the new Section 174A.
- Receive practical guidance for identifying, documenting and substantiating qualified research expenses (QREs) to help maximize credit claims in light of the new Form 6765 requirements.
- Uncover industry-specific insights, including how companies in technology, manufacturing, life sciences and other sectors can leverage the R&D Tax Credit.

Discover how our R&D Tax Credit Services professionals can help your organization maximize incentives and satisfy IRS filing requirements: https://www.cbh.com/services/tax/tax-credits-incentives-advisory/research-development-tax-credits/ 
Learn more about the Section 174 Repeal and the pros and cons of amending vs. not amending 2022 – 2024 Tax Returns for R&E Deductions: https://www.cbh.com/insights/articles/section-174-repeal-re-expensing-in-2025/  
Explore the latest updates to Form 6765: https://www.cbh.com/insights/articles/irs-updates-form-6765-for-2025-rd-tax-credits/ 

Questions? Contact Us: https://www.cbh.com/contact/connect-me-with-a-professional/ 

Follow us to hear about more upcoming events:
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/CherryBekaertCB
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/cherrybekaert/
Twitter: https://twitter.com/CherryBekaert
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/cherrybekaert

metadata.shortDescription:
Q3–Q4 Emergency Update: Post-IRS R&D Guidance

This installment of our quarterly R&D Tax Credit webinar series focuses on the latest legislative and procedural developments impacting IRC Section 41. We cover the transition from Section 174 to 174A, new documentation requirements for Form 6765, and key elections clarified under Rev. Proc. 2025-28. 
 
With updated guidance now in effect, businesses have a timely opportunity to revisit their R&D strategies, enhance compliance, and optimize tax benefits for the remainder of 2025.

In this session you will learn how to: 
- Analyze the transition from IRC Section 174 to Section 174A and its implications for amortization, elections and strategic planning.
- Interpret the revised documentation and disclosure requirements on Form 6765, including project-level substantiation and audit readiness.
- Apply guidance from Rev. Proc. 2025-28 to make or revoke elections related to R&D credits, capitalization and Section 280C.
- Evaluate how current legislative and procedural changes create a more favorable environment for claiming R&D incentives and improving cash flow.

Questions? Contact Us: https://www.cbh.com/contact/connect-me-with-a-professional/

Learn more about Cherry Bekaert's R&D Tax Credit & Incentives Advisory Services - https://www.cbh.com/services/tax/tax-credits-incentives-advisory/research-development-tax-credits/

metadata.title: Workers Comp Premium Recovery Audit
metadata.author: Watchdog Advisory
metadata.shortDescription:
https://watchdogadvisory.com  |  Kansas City, MO  |  (800) 488-5798

Worker’s Compensation Premium Recovery

Over 70% of companies are overpaying their workers’ compensation insurance premiums. Our review is provided on a contingency fee basis so if we can’t find savings there is no cost to the client. We go back 5-7 years and look for overpayments. We do not sell P & C we go in the past and recover overpaid workers comp premiums. It’s a win-win for both you and your client as you are paid on a percentage of the recovered dollars.

Workers’ compensation premiums are a significant company expense. In fact workers comp is often the third most expensive line item in a company’s P & L. Our Work Comp Premium Audit program evaluates up to the last seven years of a company’s policies and premium calculations to determine if the correct amount of premiums had been charged.

Our audit team has over fifty years of combined experience in workers’ compensation premium matters. The system that determines these premiums is extremely complicated involving many components and entities including rating bureaus, insurance company underwriters and insurance agents. When it comes to establishing appropriate classifications with hundreds of unique business classifications, there is a significant opportunity for a lower rated classification to be applied as they are constantly changing, open to interpretation and are typically determined by insurance company underwriters and rating bureaus. All aspects of the client’s workers’ comp premiums are reviewed including:

 - classifications
 - experience ratings (ex-mods)
 - payroll audits
 - rates
 - applicable discounts

Many of our recoveries are a result of improperly calculated experience ratings and/or the erroneous application of experience ratings.

Most companies do not realize that the workers’ compensation insurance company’s payroll auditor that performs the annual audit is not there to determine if your client has been overcharged (that auditor is either an employee or contractor of the insurance company to conduct the audit).

Our professional auditors are familiar with individual states insurance statutes along with rating bureau rules and regulations that affect how workers’ compensation premiums are computed.

Upon completion of our analysis, a written report is provided to the client documenting the overcharges, including supporting documentation needed to recover the overcharges.

metadata.title: How a Waste Audit Can Help Your Business
metadata.author: Everything Architecture
metadata.shortDescription:
Waste is inevitable for a business. But when approximately 58% of landfill waste can be recycled or composted, proper disposal can make a meaningful difference in a business's impact on the environment. However, without the raw data on your waste output, you can’t know how effective your current recycling and composting efforts are, nor do you have the information to aim your efforts in the right direction.

This is where a waste audit becomes helpful. By getting a snapshot of your office’s waste output and habits, you can more effectively diagnose issues and identify opportunities for more eco-friendly ways to process your office’s waste.

But what is a waste audit? Who performs one? This video will discuss exactly how you can perform your own waste audit, what you can learn, and steps you can take with the info going forward. (And we promise it’s easier than you think.)

Recorded live at the 2026 Route Consultant Expo, this special episode of Industry Insights features Amy Byers, COO of Slicker Trucking, sharing practical guidance on negotiating and renegotiating FedEx P&D contracts. 

Amy explains when to initiate renegotiation, why being in good standing matters, and how to build a credible case using FedEx’s key metric, stops per resource, rather than focusing on hours. She highlights common misconceptions around MEDALs comparisons, unique characteristics timing, and contract offers. Amy also introduces a calculator tool to compare current settlements, PCAT terms, and MISO offers to understand contract deltas and support data-driven conversations with negotiators.

metadata.author: LJM
metadata.shortDescription:
In this session, LJM Chief Supply Chain Officers Kenneth Moyer and Thomas Andersen discuss how to negotiate your parcel carrier contracts ahead of 2026 rate increases (GRIs). Tune in for in-depth insights into the parcel shipping market, UPS and FedEx pricing trends, and savvy strategies shippers can use to lock in better contracts. 

Why not let the experts help transform your shipping strategy?
Get Started with a Free Savings Analysis: https://www.myljm.com/free-analysis?utm_source=YouTube&utm_medium=Brand-Explainer

Learn where you could save money, streamline operations, and improve service based on your unique shipping profile.

In this video, we outline the different negotiation scenarios you might engage in as a FedEx Ground contractor. Whether your transferring ownership, renegotiating or buying a carve out, we take you through the ins and outs of MESOs, PCATs and updating your unique characteristics.

00:00 - Introduction
00:43 - Negotiating at the End of Your Current Contract Term
06:12 - Initiating a Renegotiation of Your Rates with FedEx Ground
09:35 - Negotiation of a New Business Opposed to a Carve Out
11:16 - MESO Review
12:08 - Unique Characteristics (Get the Form) https://routeconsultant.com/unique-characteristics
12:21 - MESO Bottom Line Can Be Misleading
12:51 - Linehaul Contract Renewals
13:30 - Final Conclusions

Route Consultant is the premier broker and consultant for FedEx Ground contractors and last-mile delivery routes. Our team is comprised of former and active contractors, financial experts, industry consultants, and genuinely awesome people. We have decades of experience in logistics operations and e-commerce investments. 
Learn more at https://routeconsultant.com/services

If you’d like to learn more about contracting for FedEx Ground and the e-commerce delivery industry in general, check out our FREE industry resources to learn more:

FedEx Ground Routes 101
This quick course is designed to give you an introduction to FedEx Ground routes to help you determine if this is something you want to pursue further.
Enroll for FREE: https://training.routeconsultant.com/courses/fedex-routes-for-sale-101

Events
Route Consultant hosts many live events for both potential investors and current contractors throughout the year, many of which are free to attend! All last-mile delivery contractors, logistics professionals, and potential investors are welcome at Route Consultant events.
Check Out Our Upcoming Events and RSVP Now: https://routeconsultant.com/events

Connect with us!
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/route-consultant/
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/RouteConsultantInfo/

upfront bonus that is one percent of your revenue for the year so on a million dollar contract you'll get a ten thousand dollar upfront payment for accepting one of those three miso options within the first seven days if you do not select one of these three mesos you'll then get seven additional days to go through a traditional negotiation now uh these are not typical negotiations like you may be used to in any other business there is a negotiator involved but they are there to make sure that the revenue doesn't move or doesn't move much even as you change the rates and propose different options so what I mean by that is that you may negotiate with FedEx to get a higher stop charge but it'll most likely come out of your service charge or your brand charge or some other category every day anything that you can think of needs to be called out and we have a template for that if that we can share with you if you reach out to us and this one is really important because it's not unique characteristics that's going to have the highest chance of improving the revenue that FedEx assigns your territory so whether you're talking about a renegotiation or just your normal year you assume that what you sent last year is still going to be saved and that they're still going to be have it when they're looking at your contract for next year I would still submit it every single year and you know illustrate anything that new that's happened make sure sure to re-highlight the unique characteristics about your territory that cost you time and money now for renegotiation beyond the unique characteristics you're going to need to show receipts or any detail you can for expenses that have increased that you think FedEx hasn't properly taken into account and the last thing you need The Shipware team doesn't want you to bungle your next parcel agreement, especially not during a Shipper's Market when unprecedented negotiated discounts and rates are available.

UPS and FedEx agreements are complicated by design.

The complexity obscures the way to best-in-class rates, leaving many potholes and pitfalls for unknowing shippers to stumble into.

This webinar identifies five common but impactful mistakes shippers make when negotiating discounts and terms with UPS and FedEx.

Led by Joshua Taylor and Adi Karamcheti, who have a combined 35+ years of carrier-side pricing experience at UPS and FedEx, respectively, and moderated by Luke Larson, a 9-year UPS vet (from package handling to parcel sales), this webinar, hosted live on May 29, 2024, will change your approach to carrier negotiations and help you reduce your parcel spending.

04:59 - Overlooked Accessorials
09:53 - Discount Tiers & Pricing Cliffs
13:57 - Terms & Conditions
20:15 - Competitive Bids
22:42 - Q&A

segments.text: Thanks for coming back if you haven't already go back and watch our last video in which
we discussed our first 5 tips for going into a contract negotiation.
Accessorials/Surcharges We recommend that you identify and calculate
your TOP 20 accessorial fees, specifically focusing on:
Total number of charges The average cost for each charge
Total costs for each accessorial fee Accessorial fee price increases: estimate
next year’s projected cost.
Accessorial fees add up and have a significant role in your overall shipping spend.
Benchmark Rates To accomplish a successful contract rate negotiation
with UPS and FedEx, you will need to determine the ideal discounts
and incentives.
This is where benchmarking comes in handy.
With Refund Retriever’s benchmarking report, you can gain access to realistic rates based
on similar-sized shippers.
Having this insight provides you with the necessary information and tools to determine
what the market is likely to yield for your company in way of savings.
Submit all RFPs & Responses in a PDF When it’s time to create the RFP,
specify your desired rates for each zone and corresponding weight range.
Determine what, if any, accessorial fees you would like to receive a discount on.
And Include dates for each response so that there is a documented chronological history
of each request.
Then, send the RFPs to each carrier.
Quantify each proposed agreement In a successful parcel negotiation process,
you will receive multiple pricing proposals from each carrier.
It is essential to thoroughly examine every proposal to determine the real impact on your
operations and spending.
Knowing how each proposal will affect your average cost per package,
per pound, per zone,
and per service level are all necessary.
Most importantly, calculate the annual savings the proposal provides to your company and
do not rely on what the carrier claims.
Once you receive the new contract, you will want to regularly quantify the changes to
ensure that you turn discount percentages in to dollar bills each year.
Review contract terms periodically We advise that you renegotiate at least two
months before the expiration of your discounts.
Keep track of these dates!
If you let your discounts expire and continue to ship, your shipping costs will rise significantly.
Frequently review factors like: The number of packages you send
How many times the shipping carrier increases rates, and how it has affected your business.
And, other areas that you feel need more discussions.
If you do not keep yourself updated on changes by your carrier or negotiate your contract
accordingly, you may outgrow your contracts and end up
paying too much.
Bonus Tip: Use a project management tool to keep you
on track and keep other team members informed throughout the carrier contract negotiation
process.
I hope this gives you more insight into what a contract negotiation entails.
If you have any questions, or if you would like a complimentary contract analysis of
your current rates, contact us at 1.800.441.8085
or visit us at www.refundretriever.com

CAM Reconciliations in Commercial Real Estate Explained
In this video, we dive into CAM Reconciliations — one of the most important (and confusing) parts of commercial real estate leases. You’ll learn what CAM reconciliations are, how they work, and why they matter for both landlords and tenants.

We’ll cover:

What CAM (Common Area Maintenance) charges include

The annual reconciliation process explained

How landlords calculate and adjust tenant charges

Common mistakes and pitfalls in CAM reconciliations

Tips for tenants to review and negotiate CAM charges

Whether you’re a tenant, landlord, investor, or property manager, understanding CAM reconciliations is essential to making sense of your lease.

metadata.title: CAM Reconciliation Case Study – How My Database Fixes the Most Common Lease Mistake
metadata.author: Commercial Real Estate Escalations Made Simple
metadata.shortDescription:
In this video, I walk you through a real CAM Reconciliation Case Study using the automated database I built for commercial property management.

You’ll see how the system:
• Organizes property and lease data
• Tracks expenses throughout the year
• Runs mid-year true-ups and year-end reconciliations
• Adjusts billing automatically so tenants end with small credits — not big surprises

This approach makes reconciliations consistent, transparent, and defensible — protecting owners while building trust with tenants.

💾 Download the CAM Reconciliation Templates & Worksheets: 
💬 Got CAM questions? Drop them in the comments below — I’ll answer them in a future video!

🔔 Subscribe for more lessons on CAM, NNN leases, and property management automation.

that translates into prata shares of

At the same time, the database tracks

The database doesn't just identify

Audisee’s parcel audit results are free for you to keep, and you can then begin the credit recovery process with your parcel carrier(s).

With Audisee, Lojistic puts the power of a parcel audit into your hands. Since you’re able to conduct both a FedEx audit and UPS audit instantly, you’re able to identify all potential parcel audit savings and proactively seek out invoice credits from your parcel carriers. Conducting a parcel audit will definitely not impact your relationship with your carrier. 

Arguably, the best way to conduct either a FedEx audit or UPS audit would be to have a parcel audit company handle the work for you. Since your only charged a portion of the procured savings, there’s no downside to hiring a firm like Lojistic to handle your parcel audit.

This is Audisee.  We’re pretty sure it’s the industry’s first free instant UPS & FedEx audit web-tool. It's a really intuitive app, but let’s do a quick walk-through on how to use Audisee.

First, you’ll need to enter your preferred email address.  Once Audisee is done doing its thing, it’ll email you a link to your audit results. Don’t worry, the results will be displayed on screen too. 

Now, you’re going to need to find a UPS or FedEx invoice to audit. If you’re not sure how or where to get the carrier’s invoices, Audisee has some helpful tips for how to do that.  But I’m sure you’ll get that figured out pretty easy. So, let’s browse for your invoice (assuming you already have them saved somewhere).

When deciding what to audit, you can choose multiple invoices all at once from UPS or FedEx …but right now Audisee won’t let you audit UPS and FedEx invoices at the same time. As soon as you’ve selected the invoice or invoices to be audited, hit the open button and Audisee gets right to work. 

If you’re auditing some really big invoices it’ll take a few moments for the tool to work through its audit checklist.  But once it does, you’ll instantly have your results. We think this is the coolest part of the process. It’s like winning the lottery.  

The findings tab summarizes and explains each type of potential recovery that was found. The details tab gives you the potentially recoverable amounts for each individual tracking number, all sorted out by recovery type. Clicking a hyperlinked tracking number will take you straight to the carrier’s site, showing you the complete transit details for that tracking number. The charts tab is a quick visual overview of the audit results. And then the stats tab gives a recap of the carrier, number of records, dollar amount and invoices that were audited.

Feeling particularly proud of your audit results? The share link at the bottom of the page can be sent to anyone in your organization. Don’t stress, we’ll email you the results, along with a share link too. And with all that you should have what you need to start the process of chasing the carrier down for your money.  Of course that’s easier said than done.  Keep in mind that the crew at Lojistic is more than happy to help!  We do it for a living and we’re super good at it. 

In the meantime… Audisee. Use it! It’ll for sure help you send costs packing.

metadata.title: How to Appeal Your 2026 Property Tax Assessment — The Step by Step Process Most Seniors Never Use
metadata.author: USA Senior Laws Guide
metadata.shortDescription:
If you got hit with a higher property tax assessment in 2026, you have the legal right to appeal it and potentially save hundreds or thousands of dollars per year. In this video I break down the step-by-step process to appeal your property tax assessment, the four types of evidence that actually win appeals, the four mistakes that cause most homeowners to lose, and how to combine an appeal win with the senior property tax exemptions we covered in our earlier video.

You'll learn how property tax assessments are actually calculated by county assessors using mass appraisal computer models, why those models are wrong in specific cases all the time, and why homeowners who appeal win or get a partial reduction in 30 to 60 percent of cases in most counties.

I walk you through the four pieces of evidence that win property tax appeals, including recent comparable sales of similar homes in your neighborhood, photographs of your home's condition issues like roof wear or foundation problems, information about your neighbors' assessments under the equity argument, and corrections to errors in the county's own records.

I also cover the four most common mistakes that cause appeals to fail, including missing the short filing deadline that is typically only 30 to 60 days, arguing about your tax bill instead of your assessed value, showing up emotional instead of prepared, and failing to appeal in years when increases are small.

Most importantly, I walk you through the six-step process for filing your appeal, whether to do it yourself or hire a property tax consultant on contingency, and how seniors can combine a successful appeal with state senior property tax exemptions, freezes, and deferral programs for a permanent reduction in their tax bill.

This video applies to senior homeowners in every U.S. state who have received a property tax assessment they want to challenge.

If this video helped you, please subscribe and share it with another senior homeowner. New videos every few days on Social Security, Medicare, property taxes, senior banking, and the laws that actually affect your retirement.

Topics covered in this video: 00:00 Why your property tax assessment may be wrong 01:30 The truth about how assessments are calculated 03:00 Who should consider filing an appeal 04:30 Evidence type 1 — comparable sales 05:30 Evidence type 2 — photos of condition issues 06:30 Evidence type 3 — your neighbors' assessments 07:30 Evidence type 4 — errors in county records 08:30 Four mistakes that cause appeals to lose 10:00 Step-by-step how to file your appeal 11:30 Combining an appeal with senior exemptions

Disclaimer: This video is for general educational purposes only and is not legal, tax, or financial advice. Property tax appeal rules vary by state and county. For your specific situation, please contact your county assessor's office or consult a licensed property tax professional.

metadata.title: Financial Modelling for Utility Tariff Setting
metadata.author: Power Futures Lab
metadata.shortDescription:
Electricity tariffs determine whether power sectors survive or collapse.

Across much of Africa, utilities are in financial distress. Tariffs are often not cost-reflective, revenue requirements are misunderstood, and fiscal pressure is mounting. Understanding how tariffs are actually built, from cost drivers through to retail pricing, is essential for regulators, utilities, policymakers and investors.

This practical financial modelling course equips participants to:

• Build and interrogate a real financial model for an African utility
• Analyse cost drivers across generation, transmission and distribution
• Understand revenue requirements and tariff structures
• Link asset valuation, budgeting and affordability to retail tariffs
• Apply modelling skills beyond the power sector

The course is hands-on and Excel-based, grounded in African regulatory contexts, with participants from across the continent sharing real-world experience on what works and what does not.

If you work in energy policy, regulation, utility finance or infrastructure investment, this programme is directly relevant to your work.

Key Moments

00:00 Why utility finances are in crisis
00:10 Course objective, Understanding tariff determination
00:25 Financial models as decision tools
00:39 Building a real utility model in Excel
01:01 Why tariff reform matters now
01:15 Cost-reflective tariffs in African markets
01:26 Revenue requirements and retail tariff design
01:49 Practical impact for practitioners
01:58 Pan-African peer learning

#ElectricityTariffs #PowerSectorReform #UtilityFinance #EnergyPolicy #AfricaEnergy #InfrastructureFinance #EnergyTransition

metadata.title: Work Opportunity Tax Credits - IRS Form 8850 & DOL Form 9061
metadata.author: Jason D. Knott
metadata.shortDescription:
The Federal Work Opportunity Credit is a federal tax credit for employers who hire employees who are part of certain "Targeted Groups" of individuals. The IRS designates these individuals as having difficulty finding jobs in the workplace, so the federal credit was implemented to incentivize employers to hire these types of workers.  Examples of such individuals include qualified veterans, SNAP recipients, ex-felons, etc.  

In order to qualify for the credits, the employer must submit appropriate documents to the State Workforce Agency (SWA) in their home state.  IRS Form 8850 & Department of Labor (DOL) Form 9061 must be completed and filed with the SWA. A business reports the federal tax credit on IRS Form 5884 and is attached to the business tax return.  

If the employee works 400 hours or more during the year, the credit is generally 40% of the first-year wages, while the credit is only 25% of the wages if the employee worked more than 120 but less than 400 hours.

For a tutorial on how to file out the IRS Form 5884 to claim the tax credits on your federal tax return, view our video here:fill

metadata.title: How To Claim Up To $9,600 In Tax Credits Per Hire - A Work Opportunity Tax Credit Webinar
metadata.author: Workstream
metadata.shortDescription:
Learn how to maximize the Work Opportunity Tax Credit Program for your business and potentially claim up to $9,600 in tax credits through WOTC for each new hire. In this Workstream webinar, Lydia Hall, Head of Growth and Marketing at Workstream, takes a deep-dive into the process of identifying people who qualify as soon as they apply, how to claim the benefits, and how the tax law has changed in 2020.

Lydia Fayal Hall is the Head of Growth and Marketing at Workstream. Formerly in corporate law, Lydia holds a Juris Doctor (J.D.) from UPenn Law School and Wharton. She’s an expert in helping over 5000 hiring managers maximize their annual tax credits through this federal program.  

Read the full transcript of this WOTC Webinar here: 
https://www.workstream.us/blog/work-opportunity-tax-credit-webinar-wotc

Workstream is a hiring platform for retail & restaurant businesses. We help companies to source, screen, and on-board hourly workers faster and better using texting and automation, while saving money on hiring. Our platform has a built-in integration with WOTC to help you maximize your tax credits in a seamless manner so you can focus on growing your business. Find out how here: https://www.workstream.us/blog/wotc-integration-new-workstream-feature

Follow us on social media for the latest HR Tips & Updates:
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/workstream-us/
Twitter: https://twitter.com/workstream_us
Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/workstream.us/
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/workstreamhq/?hl=en
Youtube: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCcwcZ2EBfqKpsOzHDhVtXkA

How to Qualify for WOTC (1:54 - 7:22)
Why File for WOTC (7:23 - 8:57)
How to Apply for WOTC (8:58 - 12:51)
Workstream and WOTC.com Integration (12:52 - 17:53)
Q&A: coronavirus Aid Relief and Economic Security CARES Act (17:54 - 19:12)
Q&A: Employees Participation (19:13 - 19:49)
Q&A: Popular Tax Credits (19:50 - 20:57)
Q&A: Availability of WOTC Credits (20:58 - 23:09)
Q&A: SNAP Qualification Time Frame (23:10 - 26:11)

metadata.title: Work Opportunity Tax Credit: A Tutorial for Employers
metadata.author: Workforce3One
metadata.shortDescription: The Workforce Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC) program is a Federal tax credit available to employers for hiring individuals from certain target groups who have consistently faced significant barriers to employment.  This tutorial provides employers with an introduction to WOTC, details on what workers are eligible and other program requirements, and a step-by-step guide on how to apply for the tax credit.

segments.text: What is WOTC? It stands for the Work Opportunity Tax Credit.
WOTC is money back for employers who hire good people who face a challenge getting a job.

You may be able to get a WOTC tax credit if you hire an unemployed veteran... or someone who has received food stamps... or has received vocational rehabilitation... or who faces other kinds of challenges getting a job.
You can get a tax credit of between $1200 and $9600 for each WOTC-eligible hire.
Getting the WOTC tax credit means doing some paperwork. But it’s really not that complicated.
You apply for WOTC by sending two forms to the Department of Labor in your state government.
It’s usually called the State Workforce Agency.
If the State Workforce Agency certifies your WOTC application, then you can file with the IRS to claim the tax credit.
And that’s it, you have your WOTC! It’s an opportunity for a deserving job candidate, and a tax credit for you.
If you think you might want to apply for a Work Opportunity Tax Credit or WOTC (pronounced “watt-see”), The next few minutes will show you how to do it.
There are five steps, and we’ll explain them one at a time.
As we go, we’ll give you tips, like this.
But first, you need to know what types of workers are eligible for WOTC.
These include veterans; summer youth employees; ex-felons; members of a family that has received Temporary Assistance for Needy Families or food stamp (SNAP) benefits;
certain people with disabilities, who receive SSI benefits or who are getting vocational rehabilitation; and people who live in certain low-income communities.
You can find out all the details on eligibility requirements at doleta.gov/wotc.
There are some people who don’t qualify: relatives and dependents of the employer who’s hiring, or majority owners of the business.
Also, this has to be a new hire – it can’t be a current or former employee, regardless of how long it’s been since the person last worked for you.
Step One. This is for pre-screening a job candidate, and filling out IRS Form 8850. Ask the person you want to hire to fill out the first page. Then, you fill out page two.
Form 8850 needs to be completed on or before the day the job offer is made.
Step Two: You fill out a second form from the U.S. Department of Labor’s Employment Training Administration, or ETA.
You or the job applicant will fill out ETA Form 9061.
With the 9061, if you can, include documentation that shows how the candidate meets the eligibility requirements for WOTC.
The instructions for this documentation are part of Form 9061.
Some job candidates may already have a different form, ETA Form 9062.
It means that an agency that’s been helping them has conditionally certified them as eligible for WOTC.
If your applicant has a 9062, you just complete the employer’s part of the form.
Step Three: You’ve already done most of the work.
Now you just send the two completed, signed, and dated forms to your State Workforce Agency.
Different states have different ways for employers to submit the forms.
You can check this website for information for your state: doleta.gov/wotc.
This site also lists the WOTC coordinator in your state – a good person to contact if you have questions about WOTC or the application process.
You must submit the forms within 28 days after your new employee starts working for you.
If you don’t meet this requirement, then your WOTC application will be denied by the state.
How can you prevent this from happening?
The minute you and your job applicant complete, sign, and date those two forms, send them to your State Workforce Agency.
Do not send these forms to the Internal Revenue Service or the U.S. Department of Labor in Washington, DC.
Step Four: Your State Workforce Agency will issue you a final determination on your WOTC application.
This determination will tell you whether or not your new hire meets the eligibility requirements for WOTC.
If the eligibility requirements are met, then the State Workforce Agency will send you a certification.
With that certification, you’re home free, because…
Step Five is filing and claiming your WOTC tax credit! Most employers file with the IRS using Form 5884.
But, if your organization is tax-exempt, and you’re hiring an eligible veteran, then you file Form 5884-C. For more information about filing with the IRS, visit irs.gov.
Before you file for WOTC, your new hire must have worked for you for at least 120 hours.
And after you claim the credit, don’t forget to keep your records for at least three years.
And that’s it! For the price of some paperwork, you’ll have helped a deserving person get a job, you’ll have a good new employee, and you’ll get a tax credit.
It’s a great opportunity— and that’s what WOTC is all about.
Learn more about the Work Opportunity Tax Credit at doleta.gov/wotc or call 877-872-5627.

Step Four: Your State Workforce Agency will issue you a final determination on your WOTC application. This determination will tell you whether or not your new hire meets the eligibility requirements for WOTC. If the eligibility requirements are met, then the State Workforce Agency will send you a certification. With that certification, you’re home free, because… Step Five is filing and claiming your WOTC tax credit! Most employers file with the IRS using Form 5884. But, if your organization is tax-exempt, and you’re hiring an eligible veteran, then you file Form 5884-C. For more information about filing with the IRS, visit irs.gov. Before you file for WOTC, your new hire must have worked for you for at least 120 hours. And after you claim the credit, don’t forget to keep your records for at least three years. And that’s it! For the price of some paperwork, you’ll have helped a deserving person get a job, you’ll have a good new employee, and you’ll get a tax credit. It’s a great opportunity— and that’s what WOTC is all about. Learn more about the Work Opportunity Tax Credit at doleta.gov/wotc or call 877-872-5627.

metadata.title: Help wanted? Businesses that are hiring should know about the work opportunity tax credit
metadata.author: Accounting Instruction, Help, & How To (Financial & Managerial)
metadata.shortDescription:
Help wanted? Businesses that are hiring should know about the work opportunity tax credit
IRS Tax Tip
https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/help-wanted-businesses-that-are-hiring-should-know-about-the-work-opportunity-tax-credit
https://accountinginstruction.info/
Businesses hanging up their Help Wanted signs should be sure to check out the work opportunity tax credit. This credit encourages employers to hire workers certified as members of any of ten targeted groups facing barriers to employment. The credit has been extended through the end of 2025.

The 10 targeted groups are:

Temporary Assistance for Needy Families recipients
Qualified unemployed veterans, including disabled veterans
Formerly incarcerated individuals
Designated community residents living in Empowerment Zones or Rural Renewal Counties
Vocational rehabilitation referrals
Summer youth employees living in Empowerment Zones
Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program recipients
Supplemental Security Income recipients
Long-term family assistance recipients
Long-term unemployment recipients
Certification requirement
To claim the credit, an employer must first get certification that an individual is a member of the targeted group. They do so by submitting IRS Form 8850, Pre-screening Notice and Certification Request for the Work Opportunity Credit, to their state workforce agency within 28 days after the eligible worker begins work. Employers should not submit this form to the IRS. They should contact their state workforce agency with any questions about the processing of Form 8850.

Figuring and claiming the credit
Eligible businesses claim the work opportunity credit on their federal income tax return. It is generally based on wages paid to eligible workers during the first year of employment. After the employer receives Form 8850 certification, they figure the credit on Form 5884, Work Opportunity Credit, and then claim the credit on Form 3800, General Business Credit.

Special rule for tax-exempt organizations
A special rule allows tax-exempt organizations to claim the credit only for hiring qualified veterans who began work for the organization between 2020 and 2026. After the employer receives the Form 8850 certification, these organizations claim the credit against payroll taxes on Form 5884-C, Work Opportunity Credit for Qualified Tax Exempt Organizations.

Credit limitations on the credits
For a taxable business, the credit is limited to the business' income tax liability. Any credit remaining above the income tax liability is subject to the normal carry-back and carry forward rules. For qualified tax-exempt organizations, the credit is limited to the amount of employer Social Security tax it owes on wages paid to qualifying employees.

metadata.title: Energy Decision #09 - Utility Bill Audits and Error Recovery | Energy Answers by TEG
metadata.author: Daniel Burke
metadata.shortDescription:
Utility Bill Audits and Error Recovery is about taking a forensic look at your past utility invoices to find billing errors, get money back, and stop overpaying going forward.
This is Energy Decision #8 in the complete C&I energy management series from Tactical Energy Group. 100 decisions. Every one that matters.
In this episode, Daniel Burke covers:

* What a utility bill audit is and how it differs from your normal invoice review
* The step-by-step mechanics of a forensic bill audit across multiple years of invoices
* How auditors check tariff compliance, demand and energy calculations, and meter constants
* The kinds of billing errors that routinely show up for large healthcare, manufacturing, and public sector accounts
* How tax exemptions, power factor penalties, and rate misclassification quietly drain your budget
* Typical recovery ranges and what a 1–5% refund means on a multi-million-dollar utility spend
* Why most audits are done on a contingency fee basis and what that means for your risk
* The difference between a utility bill audit and ASHRAE energy audits (Levels 1, 2, and 3)
* When to schedule a bill audit in the life of a facility or portfolio
* How to decide whether to build basic audit skills in-house or bring in a specialist

Who this is for: finance leaders, plant managers, facilities directors, superintendents, and energy managers in healthcare, manufacturing, government, large commercial real estate, educational institutions, and data centers who manage large utility budgets and want to stop leaving money on the table.

If you’re asking whether you should invest in a utility bill audit to identify and recover potential energy overcharges and optimize future billing, this episode is for you.

Read the full breakdown on Utility Bill Audits and Error Recovery at https://tac-nrg.com/blog/utility-bill-audit-indiana-ci-operators
If you're an Indiana C&I operator actively evaluating this decision, get your free Energy Decision Blueprint at http://blueprint.tac-nrg.com.
Visit http://tac-nrg.com to learn more and get practical tools for your facilities.

0:00 – What is a utility bill audit and why it matters for large C&I users
3:30 – How a forensic utility bill audit actually works step by step
9:20 – Common billing errors and where money is usually hiding
16:10 – Realistic recovery ranges and how contingency fees are structured
22:40 – Utility bill audits vs. ASHRAE energy audits
29:15 – When to schedule a bill audit in your facility’s lifecycle
35:40 – Building basic audit skills in-house vs. hiring a specialist
42:10 – Morning huddle questions and the Energy Decision Blueprint offer

metadata.title: Q&A with a expert in Property Tax Law -  Chicago Property Tax Appeal
metadata.author: Quality Builders
metadata.shortDescription:
Watch expert Jimmy from Sarnoff share his firm's expertise in property tax law across various asset classes in Illinois.

Jimmy worked with his father for 21 years and highlighted the firm's focus on all types of asset classes, emphasizing their extensive experience in the State of Illinois. He also discussed the complexities of predicting property tax costs due to the system's intricacies and varying rates. Additionally, he explained the assessment process, where properties are assessed at 10% of their market value and reassessed every three years. He differentiated his firm's contingency fee model from those used by non-lawyer companies and emphasized their ability to handle complex cases through various appeal channels.

metadata.title: Understanding the Work Opportunity Tax Credit
metadata.author: VA OSDBU (On Demand)
metadata.shortDescription:
In this workshop, Anika Pompey, IRS Senior Stakeholder Liaison, explored the Work Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC), a federal tax credit designed to incentivize employers to hire individuals from targeted groups facing significant employment barriers. Participants gained a comprehensive understanding of WOTC, including its eligibility criteria, pre-screening and certification requirements, credit limitations, and the process of claiming the credit on tax returns. The workshop allowed small business employers to explore how WOTC can benefit their businesses while contributing to a more inclusive and equitable workforce.

For the presentation and responses to the pending questions, visit https://www.vetbiz.va.gov/events/events-archived/ and select "View Details" for the event corresponding to the training name.

metadata.title: IRS provides relief for certain employers claiming the Work Opportunity Tax Credit
metadata.author: Accounting Instruction, Help, & How To (Financial & Managerial)
metadata.shortDescription:
IRS provides relief for certain employers claiming the Work Opportunity Tax Credit
https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/irs-provides-relief-for-certain-employers-claiming-the-work-opportunity-tax-credit
https://accountinginstruction.info/
The Internal Revenue Service today announced it is providing transition relief to certain employers claiming the Work Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC). The WOTC is a federal income tax credit available to employers that hire certified members of certain groups specified in the Internal Revenue Code who face significant barriers to employment, including Designated Community Residents or Qualified Summer Youth Employees.

The IRS today issued Notice 2021-43 PDF, which extends the 28-day deadline for employers to submit a request to a designated local agency (DLA) to certify that an employee hired between January 1 and October 8 of this year is a Designated Community Resident or a Qualified Summer Youth Employee. To be certified as a Designated Community Resident or a Qualified Summer Youth Employee under the WOTC, an employee must have a principal place of residence within an Empowerment Zone where the employee continuously resides.

Empowerment Zone designations terminated on December 31, 2020, but the Taxpayer Certainty and Disaster Tax Relief Act of 2020, enacted as Division EE of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021, permitted the designations to be extended through 2025. On May 26, 2021, all Empowerment Zone designations were extended from Dec. 31, 2020 to December 31, 2025. The transition relief under this notice allows employers to submit Form 8850 (Pre-Screening Notice and Certification Request for the Work Opportunity Credit) for these employees until November 8, 2021.

The notice also provides guidance to certain employers who submitted a Form 8850 to a DLA for these employees during the period of transition relief and received a denial due to the termination of Empowerment Zone designations on December 31, 2020, or who received a certification before Empowerment Zone designations were extended.

The WOTC has been subject to several legislative extensions and modifications since its enactment by the Small Business Job Protection Act of 1996. The amount of the tax credit under WOTC equals a percentage of qualified wages paid in a given tax year to an employee certified by the DLA as being a member of the one of the groups specified in the law.

metadata.title: 3 Rules You Need to Know About Contingency Fees (No Win, No Pay!)
metadata.author: McDivitt Law Firm
metadata.shortDescription:
Ever wonder, “What is a contingency fee?” This video breaks down how this payment structure works for attorneys, especially in cases like car accidents or workers’ compensation claims. Often called “no win, no fee”, contingency fees let clients access legal representation without paying upfront, ensuring you can pursue justice even if you don’t have the money to hire a lawyer immediately.

Understanding these 3 things can help you make smarter decisions when hiring a personal injury lawyer in Colorado and avoid surprises during your case.

Read the full article here: https://www.mcdivittlaw.com/blog/all-about-contingency-fees/

Have questions or want to know more about your case? Drop us a comment - we’re here to help!

Chapters:
00:00 Introduction
00:48 Rule 1: The Benefits of a Contingency Fee Structure
01:54 Rule 2: You Pay Nothing Upfront
04:16 Rule 3: How the Client & Attorney Get Paid
05:52 Let Us Know If You Have Any Questions

#McDivittLawFirm #ColoradoCarAccident #PersonalInjuryLawyer #ContingencyFees 

Have you been injured in Colorado? Our personal injury lawyers are here to help.

McDivitt Law Firm prides itself on its ability to provide first-class legal representation to each of its clients, in a way that is affordable to anyone. 

We help injured Coloradans get fair compensation after:
- Car accidents
- Slip & falls (premises liability)
- Workers’ compensation injuries
- Dog bites
- Defective drugs & devices
- Nursing home neglect
- And more...

Based in Colorado Springs, Denver, and Pueblo, our videos explain topics like: what to do after an accident, how insurance claims work, when to hire a lawyer, and much more.

We can handle even the toughest cases, and our team is not afraid to take on the insurance companies that might be denying you the benefits you're entitled to.

No upfront fees—Pay only when we win.

metadata.title: UPS Additional Handling 2025: How a 5‑Cubic‑Foot Rule Can Add 190 % to Your Parcel Costs
metadata.author: iDrive Logistics
metadata.shortDescription:
UPS has overhauled its Additional Handling Charge (AHC): any domestic package over 5 cubic feet (8,640 in³) now triggers hefty surcharges — even common 20 × 20 × 22 in boxes.

Former UPS pricing exec Glenn Gooding explains what changed on June 1, 2025, who’s most at risk, and how to protect your margins before FedEx follows suit.

Key Takeaways
AHC now keys off volume, not length + girth — think cubic first.
Lack of dimension data in UPS invoices makes impact hard to spot.
Shippers may need to split shipments or renegotiate DIM factors fast.

metadata.title: Demand tariffs explained
metadata.author: Ergon Energy
metadata.shortDescription: This video explains what demand tariffs are and how adjusting your electricity usage can help you more effectively manage your power bill on a demand tariff.

segments.text: In the past, most customers have been billed for electricity on a flat rate tariff,
where they are charged the same rate for electricity consumption throughout the day.
If you have a new smart meter in your switchboard that has a communication antennae, you can switch
to a demand tariff, if your electricity retailer offers these types of tariffs.
Some households may be better off on a demand tariff without doing anything,
while other households may be able to make a few changes to how they use appliances
to reduce their electricity costs. Demand tariffs are designed so each
household only pays for its share of how much demand or how little demand it puts on the
electricity network during the busiest time. it's a bit like booking flights. If you book
flights over the busy holiday season, like Christmas, you can expect to pay more than if you
were to book flights during the off-peak season. For households on a demand tariff, this busy time,
or peak period, is typically 4 to 9 pm each day. On a demand Tariff, part of your electricity
bill reflects how much demand your household puts on the network during this peak period.
To work out each customer’s demand, we look at the total kilowatt hours used in each half hour block,
and convert that to half hourly demand – rather than the highest instantaneous
demand - between 4pm and 9pm each day. The highest reading over the month will
be used to calculate the monthly demand charge. So, the more appliances you run during the same
half hour block between 4pm and 9pm each day, the higher your demand charge will be.
That's where you can make a difference. It's called load shifting.
By changing the time of day you use some appliances, and using them less during the
peak period, your household could have a lower demand charge and lower electricity bills.
Think about shifting when you run appliances that you don’t need to run during the peak period,
like your dishwasher, washing machine, clothes dryer or pool pump, and use
them outside of the peak period of 4 to 9 pm. When you need to use some appliances during the
peak period, you can still reduce your demand by ‘staggering’ when you run these appliances.
Using built in timers on your appliances, or timers you can plug into your power points,
is a great way to set and forget when these appliances run.
Once load shifting and staggering becomes a daily habit in your household, your overall electricity
bill could be lower on a demand tariff. For more on tariffs visit our website.

segments.text: Every real estate investor dreams of

that grows while staying protected from

truth. Your returns don't just depend on

keep. And that's where smart tax
planning becomes the difference between
slow progress and strategic success.
Today, we're diving into two of the most
powerful tools that can dramatically
reshape your after tax results. Bonus
depreciation and cost segregation. They
might sound technical, but by the end of
this video, you'll see how they work
together to help you preserve cash flow,
unlock hidden deductions, and position
your investments for long-term growth.
Let's start by setting the stage.
Understanding what depreciation really
means and why it matters so much in real
estate. Every property, from a single
rental home to a large commercial
building, wears down over time. Roofs
age, carpets fade, and fixtures
eventually need replacing. The IRS
acknowledges that gradual decline in
value through something called
depreciation, allowing you to deduct a
portion of your property's cost every
year. For residential real estate, this
spans 27.5 years, and for commercial
properties, 39 years. Now, here's where

metadata.title: Are There Different Types of Cost Segregation Studies?
metadata.author: Engineered Tax Services
metadata.shortDescription:
Yes, there are different types of Cost Segregation studies, ranging from the highly detailed and defensible Full Engineering-Based Study to the less precise Rule-of-Thumb Allocation, with the best choice depending on the property's complexity and your tolerance for audit risk. Not all studies are created equal; they differ widely in depth, methodology, and precision.

The Full Engineering-Based Study is considered the gold standard, involving qualified professionals who examine blueprints and documentation in detail to produce a highly accurate, audit-defensible allocation aligned with IRS guidelines. Less detailed options include Limited Scope or Statistical Sampling for simpler properties, which are faster and cheaper but may miss potential savings and carry a higher audit risk. The least precise method is the Square Foot or Rule-of-Thumb Allocation, which is based on industry averages and should be avoided for its lack of precision and defensibility.

Four Main Types of Cost Segregation Studies
Full Engineering-Based Study (Gold Standard): Detailed, component-by-component analysis by engineers, often including a site visit and review of full documentation. This yields the most robust and defensible results and is preferred by the IRS.
Limited Scope / Abbreviated Study (Cost Seg Light): Relies on less detailed documentation or a limited sampling of components. This is faster and cheaper but carries a higher risk of missing potential savings and is harder to defend if audited.
Statistical Sampling / Modeling: Uses samples from similar units to extrapolate findings across a larger building or portfolio. This can reduce time and cost but requires proper techniques to remain credible and introduces a margin of error.
Square Foot / Rule-of-Thumb Allocation: Uses standardized benchmarks or industry averages. This is the quickest and least expensive method, but also the least precise and often leaves tax savings on the table, making it highly vulnerable in an audit.

Engineered Tax Services (ETS) offers a full engineering-based study, which is the most detailed and defensible study on the market. It is important to understand what you're getting when engaging a provider, as a quality study guarantees the highest benefit possible for your property.

Which type of Cost Segregation study fits your property and your budget? Let Engineered Tax Services (ETS) discuss your options and find the right balance between thoroughness, cost, and potential tax savings.

metadata.title: It’s Not Too Late to Do a Cost Segregation Study
metadata.author: PorterKinney
metadata.shortDescription:
Most commercial property owners depreciate their building over 39 years without a second thought. There’s no problem with that approach, but there’s no tax benefit to it either.

Here’s the good news: it’s not too late to do a cost segregation study, no matter how long you’ve owned your property. The benefit gets smaller the longer you wait, but it can be corrected on your current return without amending past years.

In this episode, we break down:

📅 Why it’s not too late to do a study on a property you already own
🏢 What a cost segregation study is and how it works
💵 How a $1 million building could mean a deduction of around $300,000 in year one
✅ Who it’s a good fit for, including the “economic unit” rule for owner-operators
💰 What a study costs, and why DIY versions are risky in an audit
⚠️ The recapture catch when you sell

If you own commercial or rental property and have never done a study, start here.

Want the full breakdown? Read this week’s Tax Tip Tuesday on Substack: https://porterkinney.substack.com/
🌐 Learn more about PorterKinney: https://porterkinney.com/

#TaxTipTuesday #CostSegregation #RealEstateTax #PorterKinney #CPA

metadata.title: Cost Segregation Analysis Explained: How Real Estate Investors Save $45,000+ in Taxes Legally
metadata.author: BizCpas Accountants & Advisors
metadata.shortDescription:
Most real estate investors are leaving tens of thousands of dollars on the table every single year — not because they're doing anything wrong, but because nobody told them about this strategy.
In this video, Yesit S. Campo CFA, breaks down Cost Segregation Analysis: what it is, how it works, who qualifies, and exactly how much it can save you compared to standard depreciation.

What you'll learn in this video:
✅ What Cost Segregation Analysis actually is (and what it isn't)
✅ How the IRS allows you to accelerate depreciation legally — IRC §167 and §168
✅ The difference between 5-year, 15-year, and 27.5-year property categories
✅ A real case study: $700K luxury property — $40,360 vs. $85,600 in tax savings
✅ Who qualifies — and why retroactive studies are possible
✅ When to use bonus depreciation to maximize Year 1 deductions
✅ Why most accountants never bring this up — and what to do about it

This video is for you if:
— You own residential rental or commercial property valued at $300K+
— You've been taking standard depreciation and want to know if you're leaving money behind
— You're a real estate investor looking for legal ways to reduce your tax bill
— You're a high-income earner with investment properties looking to offset taxable income

Resources mentioned in this video:
📄 Read the full blog post:
bizcpasmiami.com/blog/cost-segregation-analysis-real-estate-tax-savings
📅 Book a FREE 30-minute strategy call:
calendly.com/bizcpas/demo-appointment
📞 Call us directly: (305) 593-2003
✉ Email: bizcpas@bizcpas.biz
🌐 Website: bizcpasmiami.com

Connect with BIZ CPAs Miami:
Instagram: @bizcpas
Facebook: /bizcpa
LinkedIn: /company/bizcpas
YouTube: @BizcpasMiami

About BIZCPAs Miami :
BIZCPAs — a bilingual accounting and advisory firm serving business owners, real estate investors, and high-net-worth individuals across Florida, Latin America, and Europe. With 30+ years of experience and 200+ IRS cases resolved, Yesit specializes in proactive tax planning, CFO advisory, and wealth strategy — bringing Fortune 500-level tax intelligence to the clients who deserve it.

Disclaimer: This video is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax, legal, or financial advice. Every situation is different. Please consult a qualified CPA or tax advisor before implementing any tax strategy.

metadata.title: Inflation Reduction Act - 179D Energy Efficient Commercial Building Deduction - Webinar
metadata.author: Regenerative Shift
metadata.shortDescription:
November 16, 2023 Webinar on Section 179D

Section 179D is one of the biggest tax incentives in the Inflation Reduction Act, providing a savings of up to $5.00 per square foot for energy efficiency improvements to commercial buildings.    Many new construction and renovation projects in 2023 can qualify for this tax incentive without knowing it.  

This @regenerativeshift5155 Inflation Reduction Act series webinar focuses on Section 179D, the Energy Efficient Commercial Building Deduction, and how your business, non-profit, church, university, or government project can benefit.

Speakers
Billy Austin, Principal, Shultz Engineering. Billy is one of the most accomplished mechanical engineers in the United States and is currently the Vice President of ASHRAE. Additionally, as an ASHRAE Fellow, he brings extensive experience in energy modeling and energy codes. 

Randy Lucas, Principal, Lucas Tax + Energy Consulting. Randy has been helping businesses navigate Section 179D since 2009 as part of his work with Lucas T+E. He is a North Carolina licensed CPA and has over 25 years of industry experience.

Caleb Quaid, President, Regenerative Shift. Caleb is a LEED BD+C with over 18 years of professional experience. He provides holistic environmental consulting around the Inflation Reduction Act, energy efficiency, and regenerative solutions.

Summary of Key Topics:
0:00 - Welcome and introductions
7:07 - Overview of Section 179D
13:17 - How to Qualify for 179D
22:56 - Prevailing Wage and Apprenticeship Requirements
27:43 - Energy Efficiency Requirements / ASHRAE Standards
34:12 - Energy Modeling Explained
37:26 - Documentation Required: How to Claim 179D Deduction
41:54 - Case Examples
48:34 - Q&A

metadata.title: Making Sense of Parcel Costs with Joe Wilkinson at Intelligent Audit
metadata.author: Amware Fulfillment
metadata.shortDescription:
On this episode, host Chad Warzecha is joined by Joe Wilkinson, Vice President of Professional Services at Intelligent Audit, a technology services company focused on reducing transportation costs through automated audit and freight recovery, business intelligence, and contract negotiation solutions.

Joe talks about the carriers’ claims that recent parcel rate hikes were to better align these rates with the actual cost to deliver the service. He says that carrier financials don’t necessarily support this price hike rationale and gives some statistics to back up his point.

He shares some stories from the tough times in 2020 and 2021 when capacity tightened, noting that the companies that came out of it in the best shape were the ones that had already diversified their carrier bases.

He talks at length about diversification and national vs. regional carriers, and how to manage the maze of possibilities in order to achieve a cost-effective solution that also addresses service requirements. 

Parcel costs represent the largest portion of total fulfillment costs, so focusing here provides the most bang for the buck in terms of savings.  Joe provides advice that leverages his experience not only as a parcel shipping consultant, but as a pricing analyst with FedEx.


Joe Wilkinson - https://www.linkedin.com/in/joedwilkinson/
Intelligent Audit - https://www.linkedin.com/company/intelligent-audit/


Learn more about Intelligent Audit at their website.


Thank you for listening to this episode of Unboxing Fulfillment – The Modern B2C Ecommerce Order Fulfillment Podcast. If you enjoyed this episode, leave a review and subscribe to keep up with the latest insights on B2C fulfillment.


#logistics #supplychain #fulfillment #ecommerce #b2c

metadata.title: Audits & Drawback: What Every Importer Needs to Know Right Now
metadata.author: Flexport
metadata.shortDescription:
Flexport Webinar
April 16, 2026

With CBP's CAPE (Consolidated Administration and Processing of Entries) system right around the corner, two topics are top of mind for many importers: audit scrutiny and duty drawback implications of IEEPA refunds.
Watch this on-demand webinar for a two-part practical briefing built for importers and shippers who want to reduce risk, stay compliant, and make the most of available duty recovery tools.

Part 1: CBP Audit Readiness Hosted by a former CBP auditor, we'll take a closer look at CBP audit readiness and the importance of data integrity as shippers prepare for CAPE's built-in compliance controls.

Part 2: Duty Drawback in the IEEPA Tariff Refund Era As IEEPA tariff refunds enter the picture, duty drawback is getting more complicated. We'll cover how refunds affect drawback calculations, what importers need to track, and what the CAPE rollout means for outstanding claims.

Speakers:
- Thanh Nguyen | Senior Trade Advisory Associate, Flexport
- Tim Vorderstrasse | Head of Drawback, Flexport

segments.text: As a three-part series Refund Retriever is examining the
details of a FedEx contract to help shippers under a fedex service agreement.
Part one covers how a FedEx Agreement is organized.
Part 2 covers base and earned discounts within the FedEx Agreement
In this final installment lets discuss how FedEx Minimum Charges and Surcharges Work?
What is a Minimum Charge?
A minimum charge is when a customer agrees to pay the greater amount of the net charge
based on discounts or a set minimum price.
FedEx will set the minimum charge for all services in the contract.
These minimums are negotiable in your FedEx agreement.
The Zone 2 - 1 pound package is the starting price for FedEx.
This year the standard minimum charge for FedEx ground is $7 dollars and 85 cents.
FedEx Home Delivery will add $ 3 and 80 cents to this amount.
All FedEx shipments will have additional fees on top of the base transportation fee.
There are basically two types of surcharges.
Optional-service fees are included when the shipper selects specific options such as
Saturday Pickup, Signature Requirements
or Declared Value.
The second type of surcharge are those the shipper has no control,
these include residential, fuel surcharge
or delivery area surcharge.
The price of all surcharges are set in the FedEx service guide,
but within a FedEx service agreement, you can negotiate to modify or eliminate the price
of these surcharges.
FedEx will give a discount on any surcharge
But the most common discounts are found on residential,
delivery area, additional handling
and address correction fees.
All FedEx ground and express packages are guaranteed to arrive on time or it's free.
Many new FedEx service agreements eliminate this guarantee, a shipper can request that
this is not removed from the agreement.
A shipper does not have to waive the right to ensure FedEx delivers packages on time,
your customer expects on time delivery and so should you.
This provision will be located in multiple sections on your FedEx agreement.
Be sure to read the whole agreement, read it twice!
We have seen a money back guarantee waiver in one section and the opposite information
a few pages down.
If you need help with a FedEx agreement feel free to reach out to us.
Call us at 800-441-8085 or send an email to us, brian@refundretriever.com

segments.text: Carrier contract negotiation is often a daunting task.
And Even the most seasoned shippers have trouble truly understanding the fine prints to these
complex carrier agreements.
FedEx and UPS don't want to lower their rates for anyone.
However, in order to keep their client’s business they know its necessary.
Here are 5 tips to consider when going into your next contract negotiation.
Bring in the competitor carrier – Multi-carrier strategy
FedEx and UPS know and understand that they are not the only players on the field.
Use this to your advantage.
It is necessary to consider how including a multiple carrier strategy in your contract
negotiation plan can bring on a range of benefits.
These benefits include more -favorable rates,
-enhanced transit time, -increased pick-up and delivery locations,
-and more.

segments.text: One of the most common and substantial surcharge fees for
99% of all FedEx and UPS shippers is the residential surcharge.
A shipper must consider the impact and truly compare FedEx and UPS applications during
contract negotiation.
This consideration includes much more than just the discount offered.
Let’s look at a few key consideration areas with a residential surcharge contract negotiation
strategy.
Different Prices for Residential Surcharges So the first residential surcharge contract
negotiation consideration to look at is the price.
In 2021, FedEx and UPS do not charge the same price.
In 2021, UPS is ten cents more expensive for ground residential
and five cents more expensive for international and domestic express.
In 2021 the prices for the Residential Surcharges are as follows:
FedEx Home Delivery is 4 dollars and 35 cents UPS Ground is 4 dollars and 45 cents
for FedEx Ground, it's 4 dollars and 80 cents FedEx Express Domestic is 4 dollars and 95
cents UPS Express Domestic is 5 dollars
FedEx Express International is 4 dollars and 95 cents
and UPS Express International is 5 dollars
Carrier Residential Surcharge Information FedEx defines a Residential Surcharge
as a residential delivery charge that applies to shipments addressed to a home or private
residence, including locations where a business is operated
from a home or any shipment in which the shipper has designated the delivery address as a residence.
and UPS states that a Residential surcharge will apply
(in addition to all applicable Area Surcharges) to any delivery to, or a UPS On-Call Pickup
request from, a location that is a home, including a business
operating out of a home.
– UPS® Ground service fee applies to UPS On-Call Pickup requests made at a residential
address.
– Residential Surcharge does not apply to UPS Simple Rate shipments.
FedEx Ground to Residence The next residential surcharge contract negotiation
to consider is the penalty applied when a FedEx shipper uses FedEx Ground to a residential
address.
Home Delivery is the service for shipping to a residence.
FedEx Ground is a service to use when shipping to a commercial location.
When a FedEx Ground is delivered to a residential location, the charge is 4 dollars and 80 cents.
So the published rate is .45 cents more expensive if you mistakenly use FedEx Ground rather
than FedEx Home Delivery to ship to a residential location.
Most discounts for residential charges on a FedEx agreement only apply to FedEx Home
Delivery.
The discount does not apply to a residential charge on a FedEx ground package.
When a FedEx Home Delivery residential fee is set with a 50% discount and a shipper mistakenly
uses FedEx Ground the shipper will be charged 221% more for
the residential surcharge.
Discount as a percentage As you are strategizing,
start to think about the discount type you will pursue in a residential surcharge contract
negotiation.
Would you rather take a discount as a percentage of the published rate or a discount as a set
dollar amount?
Each year the price of residential surcharges will go up.
They have gone up consistently since their inception.
Shippers can negotiate a discount percentage that is 25%, 50%, 75%, or even a 90% discount
off published rates.
If you're curious and want to learn more about what you should ask us to run a contract analysis
for you at no cost.
Discounts as a flat fee We have seen some UPS agreements that provide
a discount as a flat dollar amount.
In our opinion, this is not the best option.
As the residential fees rise each year, your discount stays constant.
A flat fee discount produces a lower net discount year after year.
Residential Surcharge Contract Negotiation Each part of your FedEx or UPS agreement is
negotiable.
Having a consistent strategy that is backed up by data from your shipping spend is vital.
Know what services you are using.
Know what surcharges you are using.
If access to this data is missing, contact Refund Retriever for help.
Transportation impacts your bottom line.
to lower your shipping costs today, contact Refund Retriever at 1800.441.8085 or visit
our site at www.refundretriever.com
